business_problem: HAYA Therapeutics' on-premises hardware constrained the processing of high-resolution multiomics data, leaving data scientists competing for compute and spending time managing servers. Manual synthesis of scientific literature, patents, and clinical trials could take weeks, while an on-premises AI system would be costly and difficult to scale securely.
solution_summary: HAYA Therapeutics uses Google Cloud for two linked workloads. For computational biology, automated pipelines ingest and preprocess expanding high-resolution multiomics and single-cell datasets, with Compute Engine providing compute for intensive workflows and elastic capacity for data bursts. Separately, HAYA and partner Zazmic built an in-house agent framework with Gemini; researchers use no-code visual interfaces to deploy agents that search and summarize unstructured scientific articles, patents, and clinical trials. Gemini's federated search reaches external public sources without requiring HAYA to centralize all source data first, and the resulting summaries support interpretation of discovered regulatory-RNA targets. Researchers use the outputs in biological analysis and hypothesis testing. The story does not identify a storage product, specific external-source API, or separate serving system, so those implementation details remain unspecified.

solution_components.role: Runs HAYA's intensive computational-biology and data-preprocessing workflows without the former on-premises hardware limits.

business_outcome: HAYA reports faster multiomics processing and literature synthesis, fewer hardware bottlenecks, and more researcher time for biological analysis and drug-discovery work.
